hooks.text: If Betelgeuse exploded today, it would cast shadows at night.
What happens if a giant star in Orion explodes today?
A star engulfing Mars will explode without harming Earth.

title: What Happens When Betelgeuse Explodes?
description: In late 2019, Betelgeuse dimmed dramatically, leading to fears of an imminent supernova. Hubble later revealed what actually caused the Great Dimming.

beats.text: If Betelgeuse exploded today, it would cast shadows at night.
beats.visual: artist impression of a bright supernova blazing in Earth's nighttime sky

card.small: cast on Earth by a distant supernova

beats.text: The monster star suddenly began to fade rapidly in late 2019.
beats.visual: comparison of Betelgeuse before and during the Great Dimming by VLT, 2020

beats.text: It plunged from top ten brightest down past top twenty.
beats.visual: night sky view of the constellation Orion showing red Betelgeuse

card.small: dropped out of top 10 brightest stars

beats.text: Astronomers panicked because this supergiant swallows the orbit of Mars.
beats.visual: diagram illustrating the size of Betelgeuse compared to the inner Solar System
queries: Betelgeuse size comparison solar system orbit

card.small: engulfed if placed at Sun's position

beats.text: Many feared its fatal blast was happening hundreds of years early.
beats.visual: artist concept of a red supergiant erupting with surface mass ejection
queries: Betelgeuse dust cloud ejection illustration NASA

beats.text: Hubble solved the mystery: the star had just belched huge dust.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope direct image of the disk of Betelgeuse, 1995

beats.text: When it really detonates, Earth will stay completely unharmed.
beats.visual: artist impression of a bright supernova blazing in Earth's daytime sky
queries: Supernova visible in daylight artist concept

beats.text: Until then, Orion keeps hiding the star that will cast shadows at night.
beats.visual: Johann Bayer's 1603 star chart depicting the constellation Orion and Betelgeuse
